message.content:
Here’s a quick guide on how you can stay up‑to‑date with the latest sports news:

| Method | What it offers | How to set it up |
|--------|----------------|------------------|
| **Official league/club sites** (e.g., NFL.com, NBA.com) | In‑depth coverage, official announcements, live stats | Visit the site, sign up for newsletters or follow their social media accounts |
| **Sports news portals** (ESPN, CBS Sports, BBC Sport, Sky Sports) | Broad coverage across multiple sports, video highlights, podcasts | Bookmark the site, enable push notifications if available |
| **Google News / Apple News** | Customizable news feed, “sports” category, trending stories | Search “sports” or add your favorite teams/leagues as topics; turn on notifications |
| **RSS feeds** | Lightweight, no clutter, easy to read in an aggregator | Use an RSS reader (Feedly, Inoreader); subscribe to feeds such as <https://www.espn.com/rss/news> |
| **Mobile apps** (ESPN, Yahoo Sports, Bleacher Report) | Push alerts for breaking news, scores, live streams | Download from App Store/Play Store, customize notification settings |
| **Social media** (Twitter, Reddit, Facebook groups) | Real‑time chatter, fan reactions, behind‑the‑scenes content | Follow official team handles, join subreddits like r/soccer, r/nba, etc. |
| **News APIs** (NewsAPI.org, GDELT, Bing News Search) | Programmatic access for custom dashboards or bots | Sign up for an API key, query endpoints like `everything?q=sports` or filter by sport/category |
| **Python scraping** (requests + BeautifulSoup) | Pull headlines into a script for personal use | Example snippet below |

---

### Quick Python example – pulling top headlines from ESPN

```python
import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup

url = "https://www.espn.com/"
response = requests.get(url)
soup = BeautifulSoup(response.text, "html.parser")

headlines = []
for article in soup.select("section.contentItem__content > h1"):
    headline_text = article.get_text(strip=True)
    link = article.find_parent('a')['href']
    full_link = f"https://www.espn.com{link}"
    headlines.append((headline_text, full_link))

for i, (title, link) in enumerate(headlines[:10], start=1):
    print(f"{i}. {title}\n   Link: {link}\n")
```

*Tip:* For more reliable results, consider using the ESPN API (if available) or a dedicated sports data provider like Sportradar or TheSportsDB.

---

#### Want real‑time updates right in your terminal?

Use a command‑line tool like `newsboat` (an RSS client). Add your favorite sports RSS URLs to `~/.config/newsboat/url-list`, then run `newsboat`. You’ll see fresh headlines as they appear.

---

#### Summary

1. Pick a source that matches your preferred depth (official sites vs. general news).
2. Subscribe via email, RSS, app notifications, or social media.
3. For tech‑savvy users, pull data programmatically with APIs or web scraping.
